thread:
incident-bot: [CRITICAL] Elevated 5xx and sustained tail latency for tenant ZephyrCorp (dedicated eu-west-1 pool). OOMs observed on model-runners; rolling restarts detected. Alert link: https://internal/alerts/ZEPHYR-DED-1769001234

Maya (SRE): Taking this. Paging infra and cs. @Ethan @Priya @Luca @Nina pls ack. Quick ask: is Zephyr fully VPC-only or mixed endpoints?

Ethan (Infra): Zephyr is dedicated and has a private control-plane with private connectors in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 (pre-provisioned). Their frontend is via our edge (api.zephyr.redwood.example) -> private connector -> customer VPC. So we can do edge routing without touching their VPC routes.

Maya (SRE): Thanks. Initial triage: kubernetes shows model-worker pods hitting GPU memory limits and kubelet evicting pods ~03:15Z. Long conversation prefixes + model v4-large-quant seem to be the root. KV cache growth unbounded for a subset of sessions.

Luca (Oncall-ML): Short-term mitigation available: tenant-level runtime fallback to v4-medium-quant reduces peak memory by ~40% and speeds up 95th by ~25% in our perf tests. Command:
```
redwoodctl tenants patch zephyr --set runtime.fallback=v4-medium-quant --scope=streaming
```
This is reversible and low-risk but will affect output fidelity slightly. Recommend paired with traffic split to warm capacity in eu-central-1.

Priya - Customer Success: I'm opening a secure channel to Zephyr infra now. They have strict change windows but documented emergency permission to allow routing changes after verbal ack from their on-call. I'll ping them ASAFP.

Nina (Support): Logging customer impact: increased latencies and some requests returning 5xx. Customers seeing degraded streaming. I'll surface any customer messages.

Maya (SRE): Proposed immediate plan: 1) apply runtime fallback for Zephyr to v4-medium-quant (non-destructive) 2) start an edge split to shift 30% traffic to eu-central-1 warm pool 3) monitor for 20m and escalate to 60-100% or DNS cutover only if needed. Assignments: - Maya: coordinate fallback + monitor - Ethan: prepare warm pool and edge route shift - Priya: get customer approval and confirm any constraints - Luca: observe model perf and logs - Nina: collect CS-facing impact metrics - Sam: incident owner / postmortem

Sam (SRE): I'll take postmortem. Logging as incident owner.

Maya (SRE): Executing fallback now.

Maya (SRE): `redwoodctl tenants patch zephyr --set runtime.fallback=v4-medium-quant --scope=streaming` -> accepted, rollout starting 03:26Z. Watching memory and tail latency.

incident-bot: Tenant runtime change accepted (job id: rtchg-1769001234-1).

Ethan (Infra): Spinning up 8 G4dn-equivalent warm instances in eu-central-1 from reserved capacity, pre-pulling models and warming caches. Starting edge route shift at 03:33Z with command:
```
redwoodctl routes split --tenant zephyr --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central-1 --percent 30 --strategy=gradual --duration=10m
```

incident-bot: Route-split job started (split-1769001234-a). Monitor: https://internal/routing/jobs/split-1769001234-a

Priya - Customer Success: Zephyr on-call acknowledged emergency and approved fallback + 30% split. They requested no DNS changes without a formal CR. They want updates every 15 minutes and a dedicated post-incident call.

Luca (Oncall-ML): Observability: within 4 minutes of fallback start, 95th latency dropped ~28% on most workers. A minority of stale sessions still holding big KV states. Suggest we drain problematic pods and route new sessions to eu-central-1.

Maya (SRE): Draining affected pods and shifting new sessions to eu-central-1. Note: sticky sessions will keep existing sessions in place until expiration; we are only routing new traffic.

Ethan (Infra): Edge split at 30% stable. No node restarts in eu-central pool. Preparing to increase to 60% if fallbacks hold. Also pre-building a DNS change using Cloud DNS in case we need full cutover later. Sample GCP command queued (TTL 30s):
```
gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-edge
gcloud dns record-sets transaction add acme-us-central.edge.redwood.example. --name="api.zephyr.redwood.example." --ttl=30 --type=CNAME --zone=redwood-edge
gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-edge
```
(we won't execute without customer CR)

03:55Z - Maya (SRE): Fallback rollout finished across streaming workers. Memory pressure dropping, 95th latency improving cluster-wide. Error rate decreased from 6.2% to 1.1% overall.

04:02Z - Ethan (Infra): Increasing traffic to eu-central-1 to 60% now to accelerate drain of problematic pods. Command:
```
redwoodctl routes split --tenant zephyr --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central-1 --percent 60 --strategy=gradual --duration=7m
```

incident-bot: Route split job split-1769001234-b completed -> 60% to eu-central-1.

04:10Z - Luca (Oncall-ML): After 60% shift + fallback, 95th latency returned to baseline for >98% of requests. Remaining 1-2% timeouts tied to long-lived sticky sessions that were pinned to older pods; draining cleared them gradually.

Priya - Customer Success: Zephyr confirmed user-facing errors subsided. They reiterated no DNS changes without CR. They are happy with us holding at 60% for 30 minutes and then either a plan to fully migrate or revert fallback after additional fixes.

Maya (SRE): Agreed. Keeping 60% for 30m. Monitoring. Handoff plan: after stabilization, Sam will be primary on-call for the monitoring window. I'll document timeline and metrics.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded: previous_owner=Maya, new_owner=Sam, at=1769004600

Sam (SRE): Taking monitoring ownership at 04:30Z for 2 hours. Noted action items: - Short-term: implement per-tenant KV-cache limits and eviction at 75% usage - Mid-term: add synthetic test for long-session prefixes and autoscaling validation - Infra: review warm pool sizing and pre-warm behavior for dedicated tenants

Nina (Support): Collating customer tickets and chat logs to attach to postmortem. Noting the quality delta due to fallback. CS requested a small explanation doc for Zephyr explaining what changed and why.

Luca (Oncall-ML): Recommend an alert rule: tenant_kv_cache_bytes{tenant=zephyr} > 70% for 5m => page SRE before OOM. Also adding an automated throttle to limit per-session prefix growth when thresholds exceeded.

Ethan (Infra): Preparing firewall and peering checks for eu-central-1 private connectors in case we need a full region cutover. Also prepping a quick-playbook for DNS cutover (if customer authorizes).

04:40Z - Maya (SRE): Summary for timeline and next steps: - Mitigations applied: runtime fallback -> v4-medium-quant; edge split to eu-central-1 (60%); draining problematic pods - Impact: Error rate down from 6.2% to ~0.8-1.2%; 95th latency restored near baseline for most traffic - Customer: Zephyr approved emergency fallback and edge routing; declined DNS changes without CR - Owners: Sam monitoring for 2h, Sam postmortem owner is me? Sam confirmed postmortem owner is Sam. Priya owns customer follow-up call.

incident-bot: Incident resolved at 1769004920. Please file postmortem in /internal/incidents/1769001234 and tag Sam as RCA owner.

Priya - Customer Success: Scheduling post-incident call with Zephyr for tomorrow. Will include action items and ETA for cache limits.

Sam (SRE): Closing notes: Good job on quick edge routing & fallback. Action items assigned: - Maya/Ethan: document emergency route playbooks for VPC/dedicated tenants - Sam: RCA + publish timeline - Luca: implement per-tenant cache alert + throttle - Ethan: review warm pool sizing and pre-warm automation

Maya (SRE): Thanks all. Will follow up in incident doc and move to postmortem channel.

Nina (Support): I'll add customer-facing summary and link it in the postmortem.

incident-bot: Channel closed for new messages in 24h unless reopened.
